newsitem.title: USA: Northrop signs deal with McDonnell.
newsitem.headline: Northrop signs deal with McDonnell.

text.p: Northrop Grumman Corp said Monday it signed an agreement with McDonnell Douglas Corp, valued at $1.9 billion, to produce components for 80 McDonnell C-17 military transport aircraft over a six-year period.
The agreement follows a 1996 multiyear procurement agreement between the U.S. Air Force and McDonnell Douglas to build an additional 80 C-17's by 2004.
The agreement covers fiscal years 1997 through 2002, with deliveries continuing into early 2004.
Northrop Grumman's commercial aircraft division produces the engine nacelles, tail sections and other aerostructure components at sites in Dallas, Georgia, and Florida.

The company said the U.S. Air Force/McDonnell Douglas C-17 Globemaster III is designed to fulfill airlift needs into the next century, carrying large combat equipment and troops or humanitarian aid directly to small, austere airfields anywhere in the world.
On July 3, Lockheed Martin Corp announced plans to acquire Northrop Grumman in an $11.6-billion deal.

The 80 C-17 shipsets will bring the Air Force's total Globemaster III fleet to 120 aircraft. McDonnell Douglas recently began assembly of the 41st C-17 production aircraft -- the first under the multiyear contract.

The Air Force declared the first C-17 squadron operational in January 1995. Since then, the fleet has amassed more than 50,000 flying hours as of June 1997. "Extending our work over 80 more airplanes sustains (our) position (as the number one supplier to McDonnell Douglas), and adds significant work to our business base, providing stability for the long term," said Ralph Crosby Jr, corporate vice president and general manager of Northrop Grumman's Commercial Aircraft Division.
